archetypes.name: risk-integration
archetypes.rationale: ci-decide.sh bail tokens changed from prose to short machine tokens, which is a breaking contract change for any existing downstream consumer that pattern-matches the old prose strings; needs_user_bail_reason in ship-pr.sh also gained new tokens altering routing behavior.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every call site that currently reads or matches BAIL_REASON output from ci-decide.sh to determine if any consumer still expects the old prose strings ('Timeout: 50 iterations...', 'Too many rebases...', 'ci-status.sh returned error...'). Check ship-pr.sh, ci-wait.sh, and any test fixtures that assert on those strings. Assess whether the extended needs_user_bail_reason() in ship-pr.sh correctly handles all new token variants including 'ci-local-unfixable:*' glob patterns in a case statement. Review the SKILL.md Python driver selector paragraph change to confirm the new ledger-ready keys are accurately described and that the orchestrator-side record-before-edit requirement is enforceable. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: code-robustness
archetypes.rationale: run-step5-review.sh now captures child stdout/stderr to PID-named tmpfiles under IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR with no explicit trap cleanup, and set+e/set-e framing around the subprocess call has subtle interaction risks when the child binary is missing or exec fails.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the new stdout/stderr capture block in scripts/run-step5-review.sh (lines ~1051-1088 in the diff): the PID-named files review_stdout and review_stderr are written to IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR but there is no EXIT trap removing them if the wrapper is interrupted or the awk parse itself fails. Determine if stale files can accumulate across retries. Evaluate whether 'set +e' before the REVIEW_AND_FIX_SH invocation combined with the immediate 'review_rc=$?' assignment is safe when exec fails (e.g. binary missing, permission denied) and whether review_rc could be unset or wrong in such cases. Also inspect the emit_lint_fix_ledger_ready function in lint-fix-loop.sh: the path containment check uses a shell case glob '$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/*' which is a prefix pattern, not a canonical realpath comparison; assess whether an attacker-controlled or accidentally relative CHECKS_LOG path could bypass this guard. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: FixOutcome in checks.py gained 8 optional ledger fields that are only meaningful on one specific main-agent-required path; every other return site implicitly leaves them at default, creating a fragile pattern where callers must set all 8 fields as a group or the record is silently incomplete.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the FixOutcome dataclass expansion in python/checks.py: eight new optional fields (ledger_ready through ledger_failure_detail_log) are only populated in the two main-agent-required return sites, while every other FixOutcome return leaves them at defaults. Determine whether the two populated sites set the fields consistently (compare ledger_step derivation in the Python ternary chain vs. the bash lint_fix_ledger_step case statement for parity). Assess whether the _step_result_to_ship refactor in ship.py preserves the original token-matching semantics: the old code tested reason.startswith((f'{token}:', f'{token}\n')) for all tokens in a single predicate; the new code applies that compound startswith only to NEEDS_USER_CI_LOCAL_UNFIXABLE and uses a plain f'{token}\n' startswith for all others, potentially dropping the ':'-suffix matching path for non-ci-local-unfixable tokens that previously could appear as 'token:detail'. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
